    print(name, sum(row[i] for row in rows.values())/len(rows))

# Compare corresponding displayed means across all three filtering conditions.
p5=Path('tmp/pdfs/page-08.txt').read_text().splitlines()
p6=Path('tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt').read_text().splitlines()
tiny={}; xlm={}
for line in p5:
    # Table 5 is the right-hand column.
    right=line[90:]
    m=re.search(r'"'^'"\\s*([a-z]+)\\s+((?:\\d\\.\\d+±\\d\\.\\d+\\s*){3})',right)
    if m: tiny[m.group(1)]=[float(x[0]) for x in re.findall(r'(\\d\\.\\d+)±(\\d\\.\\d+)',m.group(2))]
for line in p6:
    m=re.search(r'([a-z]+)\\s+((?:\\d\\.\\d+±\\d\\.\\d+\\s*){4})',line)
    if m: xlm[m.group(1)]=[float(x[0]) for x in re.findall(r'(\\d\\.\\d+)±(\\d\\.\\d+)',m.group(2))][1:]
print('Parsed tiny and adapted languages',len(tiny),len(xlm))
for j,label in enumerate(['raw','primary','heuristic']):
    names=[x for x in xlm if x in tiny]
    higher=[x for x in names if tiny[x][j]>xlm[x][j]]
    same=[x for x in names if tiny[x][j]==xlm[x][j]]
    print(label,'tiny higher',len(higher),higher,'equal',len(same),same,'tiny lower',len(names)-len(higher)-len(same))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem for multilingual NLP: whether Wikipedia’s reputation for quality transfers to lower-resource languages. Its broad examination of duplication and filtering sensitivity offers useful evidence for corpus builders.

The experimental scope is substantial: 51 languages, nine monolingual pretraining conditions, several downstream tasks, and complementary XLM-R adaptation experiments. The comparisons between partitions with approximately equal character counts are a useful attempt to separate heuristic scores from data quantity.

The language-specific findings are informative. In particular, the Moroccan Arabic script-switching example demonstrates a concrete failure of script filtering, supporting the recommendation to consider language and task requirements when curating data.
The linked pipeline package, detailed result tables, and appendix containing architectures, vocabulary sizes, and training schedules provide a useful foundation for reproducibility.
weaknesses: The interpretation of filtering sensitivity as Wikipedia quality is insufficiently validated. Sections 3–4 largely assume that removed material is undesirable and then construct quality tiers from removal rates. Foreign-script quotations, names, and legitimate multilingual content need not be poor quality, while same-script language errors escape this filter. Near-duplicate articles can also contain distinct useful facts. A representative manual audit of retained and removed material, or narrower labeling of the tiers as filtering sensitivity, is needed to support these conclusions.

The experiments do not establish that quality-based selection explains the claimed efficiency benefit. Both high- and low-scoring half-corpus partitions often perform similarly, and there is no random-subset baseline matched for data size and training budget. Raw and primarily filtered monolingual models also use different tokenizers. Fixed epoch counts imply different training exposure after pruning, but actual token counts, update counts, and runtime savings are not reported. These results suggest potential data reduction, but do not substantiate the stronger claim that quality matters more than quantity.

The statistical argument for preserving performance is invalid. Section 6.1 treats a nonsignificant correlation between removal fraction and performance change as evidence of no significant performance decrease; these are different hypotheses. Substantial regressions also occur, including Acehnese SIB200 dropping from 0.27 to 0.15 after primary filtering and Moroccan Arabic sentiment dropping from 0.46 to 0.40. Paired uncertainty estimates and an explicit acceptable-loss criterion are needed to support the headline claim, with clearer qualification by language and task.

The result reporting requires correction and verification. In Table 6, the three displayed Tier 4 raw_wiki scores average approximately 0.60, but the reported average is 0.66; the other Tier 4 averages also disagree with their displayed rows. Additionally, raw_wiki and +heuristic have identical reported uncertainty values in all 118 language/task entries across Tables 2–6. This systematic pattern warrants checking the aggregation and table-generation code and supplying per-run results.

Important reproduction details remain unspecified in the manuscript: the Wikipedia snapshot and extraction procedure, MinHash shingling and configuration, KDE kernel/bandwidth and the rule combining heuristic thresholds, validation-set construction, and whether the five runs repeat pretraining or only fine-tuning. Task metrics also need explicit definitions, particularly entity-level F1 versus token accuracy for NER; Figure 6 labels every task as accuracy. Together with the unresolved controls and reporting issues, these gaps prevent a clear Findings recommendation at present.
